parse_calls.instructions: Map one client spreadsheet column to one canonical Brazilian invoice column. The column names and name_confidence remain the primary semantic evidence throughout the decision; compare how close the candidate name scores are and never forget them after inspecting values. A client header can be bogus or misleading, so distinctive content and format evidence may override a weak name; generic numeric similarity alone is not enough. profile_similarity is a generic value-shape retrieval signal, not proof of a mapping. Then use representative values, inferred types, formats, lengths, and numeric scales. Recognize dates, monetary values, tax bases, tax rates, tax amounts, CFOP, NCM, CNPJ/CPF, invoice numbers, series, and 44-digit NF-e keys. First identify the semantic role of each header: a tax situation/code is not a tax base, rate, or amount even when all contain numbers. semantic_header_conflict identifies explicit tax-family or role disagreement; treat it as strong contrary evidence. A conflicting candidate may remain viable only when distinctive row content indicates that its header is bogus or wrong. Most canonical fields may be absent from a client export. Do not choose the best of bad candidates: return null unless the evidence supports the same business meaning. Matching only a broad type, generic numbers, zeros, dates, or strings is not semantic evidence. distinctive_sample_overlap reports exact overlap after excluding zeros and trivial short numbers; a positive value is strong row evidence and should be examined together with the headers. relationship_evidence contains conservative row-wise fiscal checks such as tax value approximately equaling base times rate, or line value approximately equaling quantity times unit price. A high score across many rows is strong evidence; a low score is contrary evidence, but legitimate adjustments, rounding, exemptions, credits, and reversals mean it is not an absolute rule. catalog_evidence reports membership in versioned official Brazilian fiscal-code tables. coverage is the fraction of all nonblank values found in the catalog; score also discounts short, collision-prone domains such as two-digit CST. High coverage in CFOP, NCM, municipality, or cClassTrib is distinctive content evidence. CST values overlap across taxes, especially PIS and COFINS, so use the header and tax-family context to disambiguate them. all_zero_only is not useful evidence. State, municipal, and federal registrations are distinct and cannot be selected only because their values have similar shapes. CPF/CNPJ values may contain 11 or 14 digits, may include punctuation, and spreadsheet numeric cells may lose a leading zero. Prefer a candidate that explicitly names the compatible identifier over a generic document-number field. When candidates are otherwise close, prefer the header with the same semantic role and no unrelated extra qualifier. CFOP may appear as four digits (5102) or with an ERP suffix (5102/AA); those formats are compatible. Do not choose a candidate merely because both are numeric. A profile whose evidence_quality is empty or all_zero provides little or no row evidence: zeros neither confirm a mapping nor contradict a strong name match. When row evidence is weak, keep final_confidence close to the relevant name_confidence. Return null when the data does not support a mapping. final_confidence must reflect both the name and data evidence. Keep the reason to one sentence.

parse_kwargs.instructions: Map one client spreadsheet column to one canonical Brazilian invoice column. The column names and name_confidence remain the primary semantic evidence throughout the decision; compare how close the candidate name scores are and never forget them after inspecting values. A client header can be bogus or misleading, so distinctive content and format evidence may override a weak name; generic numeric similarity alone is not enough. profile_similarity is a generic value-shape retrieval signal, not proof of a mapping. Then use representative values, inferred types, formats, lengths, and numeric scales. Recognize dates, monetary values, tax bases, tax rates, tax amounts, CFOP, NCM, CNPJ/CPF, invoice numbers, series, and 44-digit NF-e keys. First identify the semantic role of each header: a tax situation/code is not a tax base, rate, or amount even when all contain numbers. semantic_header_conflict identifies explicit tax-family or role disagreement; treat it as strong contrary evidence. A conflicting candidate may remain viable only when distinctive row content indicates that its header is bogus or wrong. Most canonical fields may be absent from a client export. Do not choose the best of bad candidates: return null unless the evidence supports the same business meaning. Matching only a broad type, generic numbers, zeros, dates, or strings is not semantic evidence. distinctive_sample_overlap reports exact overlap after excluding zeros and trivial short numbers; a positive value is strong row evidence and should be examined together with the headers. relationship_evidence contains conservative row-wise fiscal checks such as tax value approximately equaling base times rate, or line value approximately equaling quantity times unit price. A high score across many rows is strong evidence; a low score is contrary evidence, but legitimate adjustments, rounding, exemptions, credits, and reversals mean it is not an absolute rule. catalog_evidence reports membership in versioned official Brazilian fiscal-code tables. coverage is the fraction of all nonblank values found in the catalog; score also discounts short, collision-prone domains such as two-digit CST. High coverage in CFOP, NCM, municipality, or cClassTrib is distinctive content evidence. CST values overlap across taxes, especially PIS and COFINS, so use the header and tax-family context to disambiguate them. all_zero_only is not useful evidence. State, municipal, and federal registrations are distinct and cannot be selected only because their values have similar shapes. CPF/CNPJ values may contain 11 or 14 digits, may include punctuation, and spreadsheet numeric cells may lose a leading zero. Prefer a candidate that explicitly names the compatible identifier over a generic document-number field. When candidates are otherwise close, prefer the header with the same semantic role and no unrelated extra qualifier. CFOP may appear as four digits (5102) or with an ERP suffix (5102/AA); those formats are compatible. Do not choose a candidate merely because both are numeric. A profile whose evidence_quality is empty or all_zero provides little or no row evidence: zeros neither confirm a mapping nor contradict a strong name match. When row evidence is weak, keep final_confidence close to the relevant name_confidence. Return null when the data does not support a mapping. final_confidence must reflect both the name and data evidence. Keep the reason to one sentence.
